newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen sees 280 store openings in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen sees 280 store openings in 1998.

text.p: Walgreen Co, the drugstore chain, said it expects to open 280 new stores in 1998 and could add as many as a store a day in 1999.

The company said it added 151 new stores during the first nine months and is on course to add 230 new stores in 1997. Of the new stores, 43 were relocations of existing stores, and that ratio is expected to be about the same in 1998, a Walgreen spokesman said.
Walgreen said it operated 2,289 stores as of May 31.
Walgreen also said it expects to post its 23rd consecutive year of record results in fiscal 1997.
The company reported net income of $371.7 million, or $1.50 a share, on sales of $11.8 billion in fiscal 1996 ended August 31.
Earlier Monday, Walgreen reported net income of $108.1 million, or $0.44 a share, for the third quarter ended May 31, compared to $91.6 million, or $0.37 a share, a year ago.
Walgreen shares were up 1-1/16 at 51-7/8 Monday.
